email.subject: A refund of CHF 86.40 is waiting for you

body.v: According to our records, you overpaid your last premium. We would like to refund you CHF 86.40.
To process the payment, please reply to this email with your full name, date of birth and bank account number.
Refunds not claimed this month are returned to our common fund.

hotspots.explain: helveticare-claims.example is not helveticare.example, the insurer's domain.
Money you never asked for, with a precise amount to back it up. Enough to spark your curiosity, and the urge to cash in.
Name, date of birth and account number, by simple reply: far more than a refund needs. An insurer doesn't ask for that by email.
"not claimed this month": a made-up deadline, so you reply quickly.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone posing as HelvetiCare. The address is on helveticare-claims.example, not the insurer's domain.

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: The lure of money, with a little hurry: cash out of the blue, but only this month.
choices: The urge to cash in, with a short deadline

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Reply with your full name, date of birth and account number. Enough to steal your identity.
choices: Reply with personal and bank details
Click a link and enter your password

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Don't reply. Call the number on your insurance card, or open the HelvetiCare app, and ask whether you're owed a refund.
choices: Call the number on your insurance card
Reply and ask for the official form
Wait a week to see if it comes back

actions.label: Call the number on your insurance card and ask
actions.consequence: You're not owed any refund. The email was fake.

actions.label: Reply with your name, date of birth and account number
actions.consequence: With those three details, the scammer can open accounts or take out loans in your name.

actions.label: Ignore the email and move on
actions.consequence: You've lost nothing. But the email is still in your inbox, ready to tempt you on a tired day.

actions.label: Report it as phishing, then delete it
actions.consequence: Your details stayed with you, and the message won't be back to tempt you.

attacker_reveal: Nobody turns down a refund. All I asked for was a little help paying you... Your details are worth far more to me than CHF 86.40.
